meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Now the zero itself: on what basis?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing down November 2, Hale. Being put on the spot by his teacher about one phrase proves nerves, not who wrote the essay. Show me the note you made that day, and tell me what else you have.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's called writing. I'll want the outline with its date on it, and your note from November 2, in an email tonight. And whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Thursday at 8:15, your room, just the two of you, and not a word to his class. I'll agree to it to put this behind him, Hale, not because he did anything. Your email says nothing goes on file, and I want it before he sits down Thursday, not Friday.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero if it holds up and nothing going on Owen's record. I still require that the rewrite stay private and out of his class's view, and that you send me your November 2 note and his October 15 outline. I expect your written confirmation before Thursday at 8:15.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on file in writing, to put this behind Owen.
What moved her: "His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice" and the dated November 2 note, because they were specific, dated, tied to Owen's own work, and checkable.
What cost ground: nothing; your one-sentence ownership of entering the zero early took the heat out of her opening attack.
Try next time: when she asked to see your November 2 note, put it and the dated outline in front of her right then, and time your written terms to arrive before the Thursday rewrite rather than after it.
